speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how many Singaporeans are currently eligible for community care apartments; and (b) whether HDB will consider rolling out such apartments earlier to more townships should demand far exceed the pilot supply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The number of Singaporeans who may be eligible for the Community Care Apartments will depend on their age, the income levels and in the case of this pilot, we give priority to those with need for assistance with their activities of daily living.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As this is a new housing concept, we will evaluate the initial pilots before developing longer term plans.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very encouraged by MND, MOH and HDB for their collaboration to bring about such a meaningful pilot housing model and to expand the housing options for our seniors with a complimentary suite of care services – almost able to be customised to their needs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have several of my residents' families who have expressed their needs for a smaller, affordable apartments like this, with care support nearer to home.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My two supplementary questions are: one, will MND also consider granting exceptions for eligibility of such flats if one of the applicants is a care-giver below 65 years old, but is looking after a senior.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Case in point is a resident of mine who is the only child of an aged parent requiring such care that has been described in the pilot model.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is, will MND consider granting exceptions for eligibility to such flats if one of the applicants is a person with disabilities who can benefit also from such care support, but is below 65 years old?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A lot of the criteria spelt out would also be actually very suitable for people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think we want to make sure that we can first, evaluate the pilot, at least the first site, for the target group that this was intended for.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, in the steady state, we will certainly look at the exceptional cases like this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the first case, if one is below 65 years old but a care-giver, I think we can look at the situation and exercise discretion.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have actually gone to the exhibition at HDB and studied the Community Care Apartment model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am very impressed and very excited as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My supplementary question is related to Member Ng Ling Ling's question.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think it is such an excellent model and it should be scaled.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am asking if the Minister would consider working with the disability organisations to pilot this model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because the current options for residential living for persons with disability is not a continuum – you either stay at home with your own parents who are also ageing themselves, or you go to a residential home which is a very costly model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is also merit to develop a continuum of living models so that folks can afford and benefit from different tiers of service packages.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think it just make sense for persons with disability who are younger than 65 years to be given that option; so that the principle of more self reliance and joint responsibility can be manifested in the new options.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope that the Minister will not wait until the pilot is over, but to try this model with persons with disability who will be able to live more independently – do a pilot of the pilot.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Yes, we are already studying and actively looking at how and what options may be available for persons with disability who may want to live independently in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For the Community Care Apartments, apart from the age criterion, a person with physical disability may benefit from the Care Apartment model.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If a younger person with disability, and it is a physical disability, would like facilities such as these, we are certainly studying that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, of course, there other forms of disability that we may need to look at, and the availability of community based services in a model such as this.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The Minister has mentioned that the Community Care Apartment is a novel housing scheme and I think the key differentiator is that this scheme integrates – it is not just about housing but it integrates care, health and social services.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And the Minister, in his reply, has also emphasised the importance of evaluating this new housing scheme.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, my question is apart from public response and market demand, what other factors and outcome measures might the Ministry take into consideration as it reviews its plans for the roll-out and evaluate the pilot scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And therefore, in evaluating this pilot, we look at a number of things.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Thirdly, for a new housing concept like this, we also want to evaluate the new models such as joint balloting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, new models that seek to try to enable the kind of relationships that seniors would like to continue with, despite moving to a new home.
